results.title: Meta opens its ad system to Claude and ChatGPT with new AI connectors
results.markdown:
Title: Meta opens its ad system to Claude and ChatGPT with new AI connectors

URL Source: https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/

Published Time: 2026-05-01T19:29:48.000Z

Markdown Content:
Meta this week announced the open beta launch of**Meta Ads AI Connectors**, a set of tools that allows artificial intelligence agents from Anthropic and OpenAI to connect directly to [advertisers](https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/#)' Meta ad accounts and perform campaign management tasks through natural language. The announcement, published on April 29, 2026, as a Meta for Business blog post, marks the first time Meta has opened its [advertising](https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/#) infrastructure to third-party AI systems at this level of integration.

The connectors are built on top of Meta's**ads model context protocol (MCP) server**and a companion**ads command line interface (CLI)**. Together, they give AI agents - including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT - a secure, Meta-authenticated connection to live advertising [data](https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/#). According to Meta, the system provides access to "real campaign performance, ad campaign creation, catalog management, and audience insights - not generic advice."

## What the connectors actually do

The integration covers four distinct functional areas. The first is**comprehensive reporting**: AI agents can surface insights and pull detailed performance reports directly from advertiser accounts. The second is**campaign management**, which allows agents to create and edit ads, ad sets, and entire campaigns using natural language instructions - without the advertiser needing to navigate Ads Manager manually. Third is**catalog management**, enabling agents to create product catalogs, add product data, and troubleshoot data feed issues. Fourth is**signal diagnostics**: agents can access signal health and quality information to help prioritize signals setup, which is particularly relevant for advertisers managing Conversions API configurations.

According to Meta, setup "takes minutes, not days." For the MCP path specifically, no developer credentials, API setup, or coding is required. The CLI path is aimed at more technical users who prefer command-line tooling.

It is worth being precise about what MCP is. The**Model Context Protocol**is an open standard originally developed by Anthropic and later donated to the Linux Foundation. It functions as a standardized communication layer between AI applications and external data sources. Think of it as a universal connector that allows large language models to query APIs, databases, and tools through a consistent interface. Anthropic launched MCP in November 2024. Since then, the protocol has spread rapidly across the advertising technology ecosystem - a pattern PPC Land has tracked closely throughout 2025 and into 2026.

## The MCP wave in advertising technology

Meta is not the first advertising platform to build on MCP, but it is arguably the most consequential given the scale of its advertiser base.[Google's Ads API team explored an MCP server in July 2025](https://ppc.land/google-explores-mcp-server-for-ads-api-integration/)and then released an[open-source implementation on October 7, 2025](https://ppc.land/google-releases-open-source-mcp-server-for-ads-api-integration/). Amazon Ads launched its own MCP server in[closed beta on November 13, 2025](https://ppc.land/amazon-launches-closed-beta-for-ai-agent-advertising-integration/), supporting connections from Claude, ChatGPT, Amazon Q, and Amazon Bedrock.[Google Analytics released its MCP server on July 22, 2025](https://ppc.land/google-analytics-launches-mcp-server-for-ai-powered-data-conversations/), enabling natural language queries against analytics data.

The acceleration has not been limited to the largest platforms. In April 2026,[AdRoll and PubMatic demonstrated cross-platform agent-to-agent diagnostics](https://ppc.land/adroll-and-pubmatic-just-built-what-ad-tech-kept-promising-for-years/)using MCP as the connective layer - one of the first public implementations of agent-to-agent communication across the demand and supply sides of the programmatic stack. The IAB Tech Lab Agent Registry, as of March 2026, held 10 active entries, all operating under MCP.

Meta's announcement therefore arrives in a market where MCP has already become a de facto standard for AI-to-advertising-platform connectivity. What distinguishes Meta's implementation is the write access it offers from day one. The Amazon and Google MCP servers launched with read-only access as their primary mode. Meta's connectors, by contrast, explicitly support creating and editing campaigns, creating catalogs, and modifying ad sets through natural language instructions - not just querying existing data.

Discover more

Learn AI Tools

Try AI Chatbots

Try Web Tools

Meta is careful to draw a distinction between the new connectors and its existing**Meta AI business assistant**, which operates inside Ads Manager itself and provides personalized guidance, issue resolution, and campaign recommendations within the platform's interface. According to Meta, the two tools "are better together." The business assistant handles in-platform guidance. The AI connectors handle workflows that run through external tools - cross-channel reporting, custom automations, multi-publisher campaign management.

That framing matters. [Advertisers](https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/#) who manage campaigns across Meta, Google, Amazon, and other platforms can now, in principle, use a single AI agent to query and update assets across all of them, provided those platforms have published MCP servers. Meta's entry into this ecosystem strengthens the case for cross-platform AI agents as a practical operations model rather than a theoretical one.

The announcement generated immediate discussion among practitioners. On LinkedIn, Brody K., a Client Partner at Meta, described the announcement as "a really big announcement" and noted that the system provides "a turnkey ability for AI agents from Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI (GPT) to do campaign management, reporting, catalog management and signals management directly in our system."

The comment thread surfaced several concerns that are common in the advertising community when automation is involved. David Herrmann, who focuses on buying digital advertising, asked whether an agent would flag Meta bugs - a recurring frustration for media buyers managing large accounts. Brody K. responded that an agent encountering under-delivery or performance drops "could flag things to you." The response was optimistic rather than definitive, acknowledging that the behavior depends on how individual agents are configured.

Francis Teo raised a more pointed concern, arguing the connectors are "absolutely worthless unless Meta addresses the concerns officially and clearly that people are getting banned for using automation solutions." John Gargiulo, who describes himself as building "people-driven AI Ads," called that "the most important comment on the internet right here. At least for my work world." The exchange points to a genuine tension: Meta's policies on automation tools and third-party account access have historically been inconsistently enforced, and some [advertisers](https://ppc.land/meta-opens-its-ad-system-to-claude-and-chatgpt-with-new-ai-connectors/#) have faced account restrictions as a result. Meta's official connectors presumably carry different policy status than unauthorized automation tools, but the community's caution reflects real experience.

Discover more

Try Messaging Apps

Boost SEO Traffic

Audit Your SEO

Sam Edwards asked whether Claude could disable Meta's AI enhancements - Advantage+ features and similar algorithmic interventions - on behalf of clients. Brody K. replied that it should be able to, while recommending that advertisers test the enhancements before disabling them, adding: "you may be less competitive in the auction." Jenn H., a Senior Manager of Paid Media Strategy, asked whether the connectors would replace media buyers. The response from Brody K. was that the tools "will become a media buyers best friend, especially the reporting and so you don't have to use manual rules anymore."

David Parrottino asked about using Claude in Chrome - Anthropic's browser extension - as an alternative approach. Brody K. steered toward "the authorized, official connection," which is a meaningful distinction.[Anthropic launched Claude for Chrome as a research preview in August 2025](https://ppc.land/anthropic-launches-claude-for-chrome-extension-research-preview-with-1-000-users/)for 1,000 Max plan users, and the extension can interact with

results.title: What the ad-platform MCP rollout taught marketers
results.markdown:
Title: What the ad-platform MCP rollout taught marketers

URL Source: https://www.contentgrip.com/ad-platform-mcp-rollout/

Published Time: 2026-08-27T15:10:00.000Z

Markdown Content:
ContentGrip has been tracking ad-platform MCP servers since January, when Yottaa became the first ecommerce-focused vendor we covered to ship one. Since then, the story moved quickly from developer infrastructure into the advertising stack itself.

By August, Google, Meta, TikTok and X had all published, tested or launched some form of MCP-based access to advertising workflows. X's August arrival is useful mainly because it closes the loop. It is not the beginning of a new trend, but the latest point in a sequence ContentGrip has already been documenting for months.

The pattern now looks clear. MCP went from a niche way for AI assistants to call external tools into a default interface layer around ad platforms. What matters next is not which platform can say it has an MCP server. It is how much authority each implementation gives the agent, where human approval sits, and whether teams can audit what changed after the agent acts.

### Key Takeaways

*   Ad-platform MCP access moved from experimental developer infrastructure to a common interface pattern in less than a year.
*   The implementations differ most on write access, hosting model, approval gates and how directly they target advertisers versus developers.
*   Governance is becoming the real competitive question as agent access shifts from reporting into campaign execution.

## Table of contents

Jump to each section:

*   [The timeline shows how quickly MCP became ad infrastructure](https://www.contentgrip.com/ad-platform-mcp-rollout/#the-timeline-shows-how-quickly-mcp-became-ad-infrastructure)
*   [Not all MCP servers hand agents the same control](https://www.contentgrip.com/ad-platform-mcp-rollout/#not-all-mcp-servers-hand-agents-the-same-control)
*   [Why the ad-platform MCP rollout moved so fast](https://www.contentgrip.com/ad-platform-mcp-rollout/#why-the-ad-platform-mcp-rollout-moved-so-fast)
*   [What is still unresolved after the rollout](https://www.contentgrip.com/ad-platform-mcp-rollout/#what-is-still-unresolved-after-the-rollout)

The sequence matters because each launch widened the role MCP was expected to play.

In January, [Yottaa's ecommerce MCP server](https://www.contentgrip.com/yottaa-mcp-server-launch/) showed the protocol first as developer infrastructure. Its focus was real-time site performance intelligence inside tools such as Claude, Cursor and VS Code Copilot, with structured responses built for engineering workflows rather than campaign buying.

In May, [TikTok World 2026](https://www.contentgrip.com/tiktok-world-2026-ai-ad-tools/) pushed the pattern directly into advertising. TikTok announced an Ads MCP Server as infrastructure for developers to build AI agents on top of TikTok Ads workflows, alongside a broader wave of AI creative and campaign tools.

In June, ContentGrip's [foundational ads MCP explainer](https://www.contentgrip.com/ads-mcp-servers-media-buying-2/) documented Google's implementation as a standardized bridge to the Google Ads API. The crucial limitation was already visible: Google's current release is read-only, designed for account discovery, reporting and structured retrieval rather than campaign changes.

Later that month, [Meta's MCP server concept](https://www.contentgrip.com/meta-ads-mcp-server/) extended the idea from reporting toward AI-assisted campaign management. Our coverage was careful to describe it as a test and concept, because the public detail did not support claims of unrestricted production write access.

In July, [Markifact's hosted Google Ads MCP](https://www.contentgrip.com/markifact-google-ads-mcp/) added the governance layer that the platform-native versions had not made central. It supports reporting and account-management workflows, but any operation that modifies the account waits for human approval.

In August, [X Ads MCP](https://x.com/XBusiness/article/2092614843220074912) became the closing data point. X Business says advertisers can connect tools such as Grok and Claude Code, or other MCP-compatible clients, and create, manage and optimize campaigns through an X Developer Platform account.

Read together, the timeline is less about five isolated launches than a change in the assumed interface. The native ad dashboard is no longer the only place a campaign can be queried or, in some implementations, changed.

[Adobe brings Photoshop, Express, and Acrobat to ChatGPT Adobe launches Photoshop, Express, and Acrobat inside ChatGPT to streamline creative workflows. ContentGrip ![Image 1](https://storage.ghost.io/c/a2/c9/a2c929dd-49fd-47cd-9801-f80720a3d16e/content/images/size/w2000/2025/12/Adobe-brings-Photoshop--Express--and-Acrobat-to-ChatGPT.webp)](https://www.contentgrip.com/adobe-integrates-photoshop-chatgpt/)
## Not all MCP servers hand agents the same control

Calling all of these products 'MCP servers' can hide the most important differences. MCP standardizes how a client discovers and calls tools. It does not standardize what those tools are allowed to do.

| Implementation | Public posture | Access model | Control implication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Ads MCP | Official developer bridge | Read-only | Useful for reporting and analysis, not direct campaign mutation |
| Meta Ads MCP concept | Platform test / concept | AI-assisted workflow direction publicly demonstrated | Permissions and write scope were not fully defined in prior public material |
| TikTok Ads MCP Server | Developer infrastructure | Agent connectivity to TikTok Ads workflows | Positioned around building agents rather than a simple advertiser-facing assistant |
| Markifact Google Ads MCP | Third-party managed layer | Read and write with approval gates | Human review sits between agent preparation and account modification |
| X Ads MCP | Advertiser and developer facing | Create, manage and optimize through MCP clients | Pushes the assistant closer to the campaign operations interface |

Google's current [developer guide](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server) is the cleanest example of the low-risk end of the spectrum. An agent can discover accounts and retrieve structured campaign data, but it cannot modify bids, pause campaigns or create assets. That makes the MCP useful without turning it into an execution layer.

Markifact sits closer to the other end, but with a deliberate brake. Founder Ahmed Ali described the model around AI handling repetitive operational work while 'the marketer retains the final decision.' That approval gate is arguably more important than the MCP label itself because it makes governance part of the product design.

X's positioning is different again. Its pitch is that advertisers can work from 'the AI tools you already use,' moving the interface closer to the assistant rather than asking the user to adopt another specialized dashboard. TikTok's framing was more developer-first. Meta's public example was more exploratory. The protocol is shared, but the product philosophy is not.

The rollout was fast because ad platforms did not need to predict which AI assistant would win. MCP gave them a way to expose approved tools to many compatible clients without designing a separate integration for each one.

That matters as assistants become an interface layer for software people already use. ContentGrip has covered the same pattern outside media buying, including Adobe putting Photoshop, Express and Acrobat inside ChatGPT. The direction is consistent: users increasingly expect to ask an assistant to operate a tool rather than switch context, open a dashboard and repeat the instruction manually.

For ad platforms, there is a defensive incentive as well. If a performance marketer is spending more of the day inside Claude, ChatGPT, Grok or another agent environment, the platform that is easiest for that agent to query and operate removes friction. A platform without an agent-access layer risks feeling harder to use even if its underlying ad inventory performs just as well.

That does not mean dashboards disappear. Complex campaign setup, troubleshooting, creative review and exception handling still benefit from purpose-built interfaces. The faster shift is that routine reporting and operational requests can increasingly start somewhere else.

This is why the foundational June coverage focused on the combination of tool access, permissions and governance rather than on MCP as a new dashboard. The interface becomes partly the platform, partly the AI client and partly the rules that determine what the client is allowed to do.

## What is still unresolved after the rollout

The first unresolved issue is permissions. Google is explicit about read-only access, Markifact makes human approval central, and other implementations expose different levels of execution. Marketers cannot treat

Title: Meta tests MCP server concept for AI-assisted ad workflows (55)

URL Source: https://www.contentgrip.com/meta-ads-mcp-server/

Published Time: 2026-06-17T02:01:57.000Z

Markdown Content:
## Inside Meta’s ads MCP server and what it could automate for media buyers

Meta’s MCP server example hints at outside AI agents connecting to ad workflows, raising questions on oversight, permissions, and execution speed.

*   [![Image 1: Lena Marlowe](https://storage.ghost.io/c/a2/c9/a2c929dd-49fd-47cd-9801-f80720a3d16e/content/images/size/w100/2026/06/Lena-Marlowe.jpg)](https://www.contentgrip.com/author/lena/)

![Image 2: Inside Meta’s ads MCP server and what it could automate for media buyers](https://2ud5y9rdc5.ucarecd.net/e871f9f4-e8b0-4e0c-966b-7b7098833719/)
Meta is testing an ads “MCP server” concept that would let outside AI agents connect to Meta campaign workflows and help handle routine media buying tasks.

The company’s direction is framed around AI-assisted campaign management, where tools like ChatGPT-style agents can plug into a server layer that sits between the buyer and Meta’s ad systems. The setup was illustrated in an example shared with the update.

![Image 3: An example of how outside agents like ChatGPT can now help manage Meta campaigns through connecting to an MCP.](https://adage.com/resizer/v2/LWHJVFCVCBF4VGHJDXZ4TH4MCY.png?smart=true&auth=5c0e46c13b4da47759469f8d7594d4931bd8ca037e1c9b19b54be7d712152541&width=819&height=460)
## **Table of contents**

Jump to each section:

*   [What Meta’s ads MCP server suggests about AI-assisted buying](https://www.contentgrip.com/meta-ads-mcp-server/#what-meta%E2%80%99s-ads-mcp-server-suggests-about-ai-assisted-buying)
*   [Where AI agents could fit into day-to-day Meta campaign work](https://www.contentgrip.com/meta-ads-mcp-server/#where-ai-agents-could-fit-into-day-to-day-meta-campaign-work)
*   [What this means for marketers](https://www.contentgrip.com/meta-ads-mcp-server/#what-this-means-for-marketers)

The core idea is an integration layer where an external AI agent can connect to Meta advertising workflows via an MCP server, rather than operating only as a standalone assistant.

Even with limited public detail in the extracted material, the direction matters because it signals a shift from “AI helps you think” to “AI can connect to systems.” For media teams, that distinction is often the line between a chat-based helper and a tool that can participate in execution.

[Ads MCP servers and the future of agent-led reporting MCP servers give AI agents a standard way to query ad performance data. Here’s what read-only access implies for reporting and governance. ![Image 4](https://storage.ghost.io/c/a2/c9/a2c929dd-49fd-47cd-9801-f80720a3d16e/content/images/icon/CG-icon-1-1915.png)Editorial Team ContentGrip ![Image 5](https://2ud5y9rdc5.ucarecd.net/117488eb-5aa3-43ee-8207-bcc041c058ff/)](https://www.contentgrip.com/ads-mcp-servers-media-buying-2/)
If outside agents can reliably interface with campaign management, the most immediate impact is on repetitive operational tasks that slow down performance teams. In practice, that could include translating instructions into structured actions inside a campaign workflow, or helping coordinate the steps that buyers already do across planning, setup, and iteration.

The example positioning also implies a future where buyers may supervise an AI agent that handles more of the back-and-forth inside the platform, while humans focus on strategy, creative direction, and accountability.

At the same time, any “agent-to-platform” connectivity raises practical questions for teams: what permissions are granted, what changes can be made automatically, and how auditability is handled when the instruction path is an AI interface rather than a human clicking through a UI.

## **What this means for marketers**

AI agents connecting to ad workflows is best read as an operational shift, not a guarantee of better performance by itself. The value comes from reducing friction in execution and making iteration cycles faster.

1.   **Agent connectivity is the real milestone, not chat-based advice**  
When an AI tool can connect to the workflow layer, it can potentially reduce the time between intent (what the buyer wants) and action (what gets built or changed).
2.   **Teams should expect new governance needs around access and oversight**  
If an outside agent can help “manage campaigns,” the organization will need clear rules for permissions, approvals, and change logging.
3.   **Speed gains will likely show up first in routine work, not strategy**  
The earliest wins are usually in repetitive steps that are easy to standardize. Strategy and creative judgment remain human-led.
4.   **Media buying roles may shift toward supervision and QA**  
As more execution becomes agent-assisted, buyers may spend more time reviewing, validating, and steering, rather than manually performing every step.

This kind of integration direction also reframes how martech and adtech teams evaluate AI. The question becomes less about whether an assistant can generate good suggestions and more about whether it can safely interact with production systems.

Over time, marketers that build strong review loops, permission models, and documentation practices will be better positioned to benefit from workflow-connected AI, while avoiding “automation without accountability.”

results.title: The State of Advertising MCPs in 2026
results.markdown:
Title: The State of Advertising MCPs in 2026

URL Source: https://www.markifact.com/blog/state-of-advertising-mcps

Published Time: 2026-07-15T05:30:22+00:00

Markdown Content:
Seven of the 11 major ad platforms in this review have launched, piloted, or announced an official Ads MCP server. Only four can be used today without joining an alpha or waitlist, and just three offer meaningful campaign writes.

**Last verified: July 15, 2026**

The short version is that official Ads MCP support is arriving quickly, but “official” does not yet mean mature, public, or read/write. Google Ads is deliberately read-only, Meta and Amazon are in beta, Microsoft Advertising is an open pilot, Pinterest is working through alpha partners, and Snapchat has announced its direction without publishing a self-serve setup.

This report separates products you can connect now from pilots and announcements. It also distinguishes an official platform server from a cross-platform [advertising MCP such as Markifact](https://www.markifact.com/mcp), because the two solve different problems.

## Ads MCP status by platform

| Ad platform | Official Ads MCP status | Access | Authentication or setup | Main limitation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Google Ads](https://www.markifact.com/google-ads-mcp) | Available, official open-source server | Read-only | Google Ads developer token plus Google OAuth or ADC | Three core tools; no campaign changes |
| [Meta Ads](https://www.markifact.com/meta-ads-mcp) | Open beta | Read/write | Hosted server with Meta Business OAuth | Beta eligibility and account permissions apply |
| [TikTok Ads](https://www.markifact.com/tiktok-ads-mcp) | Available through Agentic Hub | Read/write | TikTok for Business authorization | Availability can vary by account |
| [Amazon Ads](https://www.markifact.com/amazon-ads-mcp) | Open beta | Read/write | Active Amazon Ads API credentials | Limited to Amazon Ads partners |
| [Microsoft Advertising](https://www.markifact.com/microsoft-ads-mcp) | Open pilot | Read-only | Pilot onboarding; major MCP clients supported | Waitlist and no writes at launch |
| [Pinterest Ads](https://www.markifact.com/pinterest-ads-mcp) | Alpha partner program | Read-oriented | Access through selected alpha partners | Not a broad self-serve release |
| [Snapchat Ads](https://www.markifact.com/snapchat-ads-mcp) | Announced | Read/write intent | Public setup not documented | No public tool catalog or launch access |
| [OpenAI Ads](https://www.markifact.com/openai-ads-mcp) | No official MCP found | Not applicable | Ads Manager beta and APIs are separate | No platform-owned Ads MCP located |
| [Apple Ads](https://www.markifact.com/apple-ads-mcp) | No official MCP found | Not applicable | Apple Ads API OAuth is separate | No platform-owned Ads MCP located |
| [LinkedIn Ads](https://www.markifact.com/linkedin-ads-mcp) | No official MCP found | Not applicable | LinkedIn Marketing API access is separate | No platform-owned Ads MCP located |
| [Reddit Ads](https://www.markifact.com/reddit-ads-mcp) | No official MCP found | Not applicable | Reddit Ads API credentials are separate | No platform-owned Ads MCP located |

“No official MCP found” is intentionally precise. It means I could not locate a server published or operated by the platform owner on the verification date. It does not mean third-party Ads MCP servers are unavailable.

![Image 1: The official Ads MCP status matrix for 11 major advertising platforms](https://storage.googleapis.com/markifact/public/images/d35b382d-ac50-4cf1-b13f-d6e8b45abd26.webp)

Official Ads MCP availability, access level, and maturity across the platforms reviewed.

## What counts as an official Ads MCP?

For this report, an Ads MCP is official only when the ad platform publishes, operates, or formally announces it. A community GitHub project that wraps an official API can still be useful, but it belongs in a different category.

I used five maturity labels:

1.   **Available:** a qualifying advertiser can follow public documentation and connect it now.
2.   **Open beta:** the server is live, but features, eligibility, or support can still change.
3.   **Open pilot:** the platform is onboarding a limited group through a pilot or waitlist.
4.   **Alpha or announced:** selected partners can test it, or the company has described the product without publishing broad access.
5.   **No official MCP found:** the platform has an API or ad product, but no first-party Ads MCP was located.

This distinction matters because a launch headline can hide the operational details. A read-only local server that needs developer credentials is very different from a hosted OAuth server that can create or edit campaigns.

## Official Ads MCPs with meaningful write access

### Meta Ads

[Meta introduced its official Ads AI connectors](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/meta-ads-ai-connectors) in open beta on April 29, 2026. The hosted connection uses Meta Business OAuth and supports both reporting and campaign-management workflows, making it one of the most complete official Ads MCP releases in this review.

It is still a beta. Access to an ad account and the actions available through it remain subject to Meta permissions and product eligibility. Meta’s official announcement is the source of truth for the current program, and the [Meta Ads to ChatGPT guide](https://www.markifact.com/blog/how-to-connect-meta-ads-to-chatgpt) shows the practical connection flow.

### TikTok Ads

[TikTok announced Ads MCP and agent skills](https://newsroom.tiktok.com/tiktok-world-26-eu?lang=en-150) at TikTok World, then launched its [Agentic Hub](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/blog/tiktok-agentic-hub-ai-agents-skills-mcp) on June 30. The official server covers campaign management, performance reporting, audience configuration, and creative operations.

This is a genuine read/write Ads MCP, not just a reporting bridge. The main caveat is access: the exact tools and availability can depend on the advertiser account and the TikTok for Business rollout.

### Amazon Ads

Amazon’s [official Ads MCP server](https://advertising.amazon.com/library/news/amazon-ads-mcp-server-open-beta) entered open beta on February 2, 2026. It can create, update, and delete campaigns, run reports, manage account settings, and access billing and financial data.

Amazon is also the clearest example of an official server packaging complete advertising workflows rather than only exposing raw API calls. Its Sponsored Products workflow can assemble a campaign that is ready for human review and approval. The limitation is that the beta is available to Amazon Ads partners with active API credentials, not every advertiser with a console login.

## The official Google Ads MCP is read-only

Google’s [official Google Ads MCP server](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/developer-toolkit/mcp-server) is available as an open-source Python project. It uses a Google Ads developer token and Google credentials, and it currently exposes three core tools for listing accessible customers, running searches, and retrieving resource metadata.

The design is deliberately read-only. It can inspect accounts and query performance through the Google Ads API, but it cannot create a campaign, pause an ad, change a bid, or update a budget.

That makes Google Ads useful for audits and reporting while keeping execution outside the server. It also illustrates why “has an official Ads MCP” is not enough information for a media buyer. Access level is the more important column.

## Open pilots, alpha programs, and announcements

### Microsoft Advertising

Microsoft announced its [Advertising MCP server](https://about.ads.microsoft.com/en/solutions/technology/agentic-commerce/mcp-server) as an open pilot on June 17, 2026. At launch it provides read-only access to campaigns, ad groups, ads, keywords, and performance metrics, with support planned for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP clients.

The public page still directs advertisers toward pilot or waitlist access. Microsoft deserves credit for documenting the entity and metric coverage clearly, but it should not yet be described as broadly self-serve or read/write.

### Pinterest Ads

Pinterest announced its [official MCP work](https://newsroom.pinterest.com/en-ca/news/cannes-2026/) on June 17 with alpha partners including agencies and ad-tech platforms. The initial use cases emphasize campaign analytics, keyword insights, planning, and analysis.

results.markdown:
Title: How to advertise from ChatGPT with no ad accounts (2026)

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/advertise-from-chatgpt

Published Time: 2026-11-03T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
AI Assistants

## How to advertise your business from ChatGPT (no ad accounts needed), 2026

What ChatGPT can do with Adwave on each plan, how to connect it, what it costs, and what to do if your plan can only read.

**Last updated:** November 3, 2026

You can run ads from ChatGPT without opening any ad accounts, but launching depends on your ChatGPT plan. Adwave connects to ChatGPT as a custom MCP server, makes the ads from your website, and buys media on streaming TV, Meta, Google Search, YouTube, Reddit and the web from a prepaid wallet, starting at $30 a day. ChatGPT gives custom servers full write access only on Business and Enterprise workspaces, so the full flow needs one of those, or Codex.

## This guide is about advertising with ChatGPT

Here, ChatGPT is the place you give instructions, and your ads run on TV, search and social. OpenAI also sells ad space inside ChatGPT through its own Ads Manager, which is a separate product. If you want your ad to appear in ChatGPT conversations, read [advertising on ChatGPT vs advertising with ChatGPT](https://adwave.com/resources/advertising-on-chatgpt-vs-with-chatgpt/).

## What each ChatGPT plan can do

This table follows [OpenAI’s help article on custom MCP servers](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt), checked November 2, 2026.

| ChatGPT plan | What OpenAI documents | What that means with Adwave |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business | Full MCP support. Only admins and owners can create and publish custom servers | An admin or owner adds Adwave. It can build, launch and change campaigns |
| Enterprise or Edu | Full MCP support. Admins and owners can add servers and can grant permission to selected members | Same as Business, once someone with permission adds it |
| Pro | Custom MCP servers with read and fetch permissions only | It can read your account. It can’t launch or change campaigns |
| Other individual plans | Not listed for full MCP | Don’t plan on launching from chat |

As of the date above, Adwave isn’t listed in ChatGPT’s plugin directory, so ChatGPT won’t suggest it on its own. You add it yourself with the server URL.

## How to connect Adwave to ChatGPT

The server URL is `https://waverunner.adwave.com/api/mcp`.

1.   In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins and select the plus button, then **Add custom MCP server**.
2.   Enter a name, such as Adwave, and paste the server URL.
3.   Choose OAuth for authentication, review the risk warning, and create the plugin.
4.   Sign in to Adwave in the window that opens. If you’re new, create your account there with your email.

The [ChatGPT setup page](https://adwave.com/help/mcp/chatgpt/) has the same steps with the details for admins.

## What happens after you connect

Start with a request in your own words. For example: “Advertise my bakery from its website with $40 a day around Austin.”

1.   **Adwave reads your website.** It suggests the customers worth reaching and makes the ads for each channel. You don’t need a video or any creative of your own.
2.   **You review the plan.** Ask ChatGPT to show the ads, audience, locations, channels and daily budget, and to change anything you don’t like.
3.   **You add money if the wallet is empty.** New accounts start with an empty wallet. ChatGPT gives you a link to a hosted Stripe checkout page, and you pay there, never in the chat.
4.   **You confirm the launch.** Every tool that spends is marked destructive, which tells ChatGPT to ask you first. Before that, the assistant can check what launching would do without doing it.
5.   **Your ads go to each channel for review.** They usually start within a few hours.

Later you can ask how the ads are doing, or ask ChatGPT to pause or change a campaign. Everything also shows up in the Adwave app.

## What it costs

Connecting ChatGPT to Adwave is free. Ads start at $30 a day from a prepaid wallet, with no contract.

*   Launching or resuming a campaign sets the day’s budget aside from your wallet.
*   The next morning you’re charged for what ran, never more than the amount set aside.
*   Card top-ups add the processing fee shown at checkout.
*   A daily budget repeats until you pause or end the campaign.
*   Extra ads made through an assistant can be billed from the wallet at published prices. Ask for the quote before you approve.

See [Adwave pricing](https://adwave.com/pricing/) for the current numbers.

## If your plan can only read

You have three options.

*   **Use Codex.** Codex can add Adwave with one command and use its write tools. It’s a tool for developers, so it’s a better fit if you’re comfortable in a terminal. See the [Codex setup page](https://adwave.com/help/mcp/codex/).
*   **Use another assistant.**[Claude works as a custom connector](https://adwave.com/resources/advertise-with-claude/), including one connector on its Free plan.
*   **Launch in the Adwave app and read in ChatGPT.**[Start from your website](https://adwave.com/#website) in the app, then use your read access in ChatGPT to ask how the campaigns are doing.

## Limits

*   **Plans:** on the plans OpenAI doesn’t list for full MCP, ChatGPT can’t launch through a custom server. Nothing on Adwave’s side changes that.
*   **Markets:** campaigns run in the US and Canada only.
*   **Channels:** streaming TV, Meta (Facebook and Instagram), Google Search, YouTube, Reddit and the web. TikTok is opt-in early access. Pinterest is coming soon.
*   **Channel mix:** which channels a campaign uses depends on its budget, audience, creative and each channel’s advertising policy, so one campaign may not run everywhere.
*   **Not covered:** Adwave doesn’t do organic social posting, email newsletters or SEO.
*   **Results:** forecasts are estimates, and Adwave doesn’t guarantee sales or a return on spend.

If you’re weighing the risk of letting an assistant near your budget, read [the guardrails to look for](https://adwave.com/resources/is-it-safe-to-let-ai-spend-ad-budget/). All of our assistant guides are on the [AI assistants page](https://adwave.com/resources/ai-assistants/).

Try Adwave free

## Start with your website.

Enter your site and Adwave builds ads for TV, search, social, and the web. Pick a daily budget when you are ready.

[Try Adwave free](https://adwave.com/#website)

Free to analyze. See your plan before you spend.

Title: Connecting Universal Ads to Your AI Tools: The Universal Ads MCP Beta

URL Source: https://www.universalads.com/blog/connecting-universal-ads-to-your-ai-tools

Published Time: 2026-09-15T13:32:22.000Z

Markdown Content:
![Image 1: Dark interface showing Universal Ads campaign stats: 4.2M impressions, 1.8M reach, 98.7% completion rate.](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/67531bf977554bf997f89ef9/6a04860d97444766aa461068_ua_mcp_terminal_v3.jpg)

‍

Universal Ads was built on the idea that TV advertising needs to be as easy and accessible as search and social. A big part of that is meeting advertisers and developers where they already work; increasingly, that means AI tools.

As the industry turns to AI-powered workflows, teams are integrating tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini* into their day-to-day. We've been thinking hard about what it means for Universal Ads to show up natively in those environments, and today we're sharing an early look at where we're headed.

## **Built API-first from the start**

Everything we're building in the AI space starts with our existing foundation: The Universal Ads Marketing API. From day one, Universal Ads was built API-first, meaning every core capability – from campaign management to reporting to audience targeting – is accessible programmatically. This was an intentional platform design before we even wrote our first line of code.

Partners like [Koddi,](https://koddi.com/)[SearchKings,](https://searchkings.ca/)[Northbeam,](https://www.northbeam.io/) and [Spaceback](https://www.spaceback.com/) have already built on top of the Marketing API to power their own TV advertising solutions. That same infrastructure is what makes extending Universal Ads into new surfaces, like the AI tools developers use every day, possible.

## **Introducing our first step: A local MCP for Universal Ads**

Today, we're releasing a local MCP (Model Context Protocol, an open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources) connector as an extension of our existing developer toolkit. This provides a standardized way to connect Universal Ads to the AI tools you're already using.

This first release is built specifically for technically-minded partners and developers who want to start experimenting with how Universal Ads data surfaces inside their AI workflows. With this initial release you’ll be able to pull Universal Ads campaign data directly into your AI environments of choice. That includes:

*   **Campaign reporting** — query performance data in natural language **‍**
*   **Campaign hierarchy** — understand the structure of your campaigns, ad sets, and creatives **‍**
*   **Insights and optimization guidance** — surface opportunities through conversational prompts **‍**
*   **Data visualization support** — explore campaign data in new ways through your AI tool 

We’re also testing AI connectors that would enable creating, launching, and optimizing campaigns. But we want to first get this version into your hands, so we can learn how you're using it and build from there. If you’re interested in getting early access to future releases, please reach out.

**Why we're starting here**

We're investing in making Universal Ads a native part of the AI tools you use every day. This MCP is our first step toward that vision. A sneak peek at what becomes possible when you can talk to your TV campaigns the same way you'd ask an AI tool anything else.

If you’re interested in speaking with someone from our team about ways you can begin using the MCP, visit us [here](https://www.universalads.com/mcp#MCP-Sign-up-form). If you’re ready to start building on your own, visit GitHub [here](https://github.com/Universal-Ads/universal-ads-mcp) for setup instructions and let us know what you build.

results.title: Introducing AI Agent Ad Buying: A New Way to Transact in TV
results.markdown:
Title: Introducing AI Agent Ad Buying: A New Way to Transact in TV

URL Source: https://www.universalads.com/blog/ai-agent-ad-buying

Published Time: 2026-09-02T18:36:07.545Z

Markdown Content:
‍

Even in 2026, much of TV advertising is still powered by manual workflows, static deals, and delayed buying signals. Securing custom content packages from a premium publisher means many phone calls, weeks of back-and-forth, rigorous vetting, and purchase minimums high enough to shut out everyone but the largest brands. This model wasn't built for modern marketers operating in a world driven by real-time data and performance.

At Universal Ads, we’ve always been committed to removing the barriers to entry to premium TV for smaller and digital-first brands. That’s why today we’re launching a new approach to TV advertising for brands of all sizes, powered by agentic buying tools.

Through a new partnership with FOX Advertising, we’re introducing AI Agent ad buying where AI agents could represent buyers and sellers directly. The new workflow, powered by humans and executed by agents, will enable those brands without direct relationships to access premium TV content in ways that were previously unavailable.

> ‍_“We’re thrilled to partner with Universal Ads to take the first step in agent-to-agent ad buying. This collaboration unlocks new possibilities for advertisers of all sizes, making premium FOX inventory more accessible and dynamic than ever before. Together, we are redefining what’s possible in TV advertising.” - Stephano Kim, Chief Strategy & Operations Officer, Fox Advertising_

## **Why we’re changing how TV buying works**

From the outside, today’s experience looks simple. Advertisers set up a campaign, activate it, and receive reporting.

But behind the scenes, accessing premium publisher inventory, especially custom deals, often involves more coordination:

*   Buyers need to go through comprehensive manual vetting to ensure they’re legitimate 
*   Custom deals typically involve frequent communication with publishers, including manual negotiation 
*   Deals must be created, validated, and passed between systems 
*   Custom packaging takes time and operational effort 

Many advertisers, especially smaller ones, are excluded due to high-budget minimums, time-intensive negotiations, or a lack of established trust and direct relationships with publishers. And even after navigating these barriers, advertisers are still often stuck with choosing from pre-defined inventory, and not inventory built specifically for their campaign goals.

## **A new approach: AI Agent Ad Buying**

Agent-to-Agent ad buying can remove these barriers by enabling AI agents to transact directly on behalf of buyers and sellers. A buyer agent understands the advertiser’s brand, goals, audience, and budget, while a seller agent understands inventory, pricing, and performance. Together, they build and negotiate custom packages in real time.

This unlocks a new level of access for advertisers, allowing them to align directly with specific networks and programming instead of relying on generalized inventory or high-touch, manual processes.

Purpose-built for content-led, publisher-direct transactions, Agent-to-Agent buying can deliver premium, unique packages designed around the brand, not just efficient delivery.

While the teams continue to define strategy, build relationships, and guide creative direction, agents facilitate the transaction. Guardrails, along with human oversight, ensure quality execution and alignment with brand standards.

With AI Agent ad buying, advertisers can expect:

*   **Direct access to premium publishers**  
Advertisers can transact more directly with publishers like FOX with less manual back-and-forth, while still building and maintaining meaningful relationships. **‍**
*   **Custom packages, not pre-built inventory**  
Each campaign is matched to a tailored inventory package based on the brand and its goals. For example, a commercial real estate advertiser can be matched specifically to business, finance, and news programming. **‍**
*   **No manual deal setup or negotiation**  
Packaging, pricing, and deal creation happen automatically between agents, streamlining a traditionally high-touch process. **‍**
*   **Scalable access to tailored inventory**  
Each advertiser gets a distinct deal built for them. What used to require hands-on work can now scale across many advertisers. 
*   **Trusted, secure environments at scale**  
With a strong emphasis on security, advertisers of all sizes can securely purchase premium TV advertising from trusted publishers. 

Importantly, this model is designed to enhance, not replace, the relationships that are core to the TV ecosystem. Direct partnerships between advertisers and publishers remain critical to how ads and placements are designed, curated, and aligned to brands. Agent-to-Agent buying can preserve those relationships while streamlining the transactional aspects of ad buying.

## **How it works**

This model builds on the infrastructure Universal Ads has invested in from day one.

Advertisers are verified through Universal Ads’ AI-enabled onboarding and risk process, and Universal Ads manages payments and billing so that publishers can have confidence that every buyer from UA is vetted and trusted, with trust being the key element for any multi-party transaction.

From there:

1.   **Campaign setup**  
The advertiser defines objectives, targeting, and budget using the Ads Manager, [API](https://developers.universalads.com/), or [MCP](https://www.universalads.com/mcp). **‍**
2.   **Agent communication**  
The buyer agent shares campaign and advertiser details with the publisher’s agent. **‍**
3.   **Inventory packaging**  
The publisher agent can propose a tailored inventory package. **‍**
4.   **Dynamic negotiation**  
Buyer and seller agents can iterate in real time to finalize pricing and packaging. **‍**
5.   **Activation and delivery**  
The deal is generated, applied to the campaign, and activated automatically. 

‍  
What historically took days or weeks is reduced to a single automated flow.

## **From pilot to practice**

To bring this to life, we partnered with FOX Advertising and worked with Crexi, a commercial real estate marketplace, as the first advertiser. While FOX inventory had always been of interest to Crexi, the time and effort required to access custom packages made it difficult to justify through traditional buying workflows. With AI Agent ad buying, that barrier was removed.

In this pilot:

*   Crexi built a campaign using Universal Ads APIs and MCP 
*   Buyer and seller agents shared campaign details and proposed options 
*   A custom package aligned to Crexi’s goals was negotiated and finalized 
*   The campaign was activated and began delivering 

What would have previously required weeks of coordination and manual negotiation was completed in minutes, making access to premium FOX inventory as seamless as activating a campaign on social platforms. Three parties, one coordinated workflow, completed in minutes.

> _"Partnering with FOX and Universal Ads on this agentic pilot has given Crexi an opportunity to explore a more streamlined approach to accessing premium TV inventory. The ability to activate campaigns more efficiently and align them with our marketing objectives represents an exciting evolution in the TV advertising landscape. We're looking forward to learning from the results of this pilot and better understanding how solutions like this can help brands like ours connect with relevant audiences in new ways." - Sandra Carvalho, Chief Marketing Officer, Crexi_

## **Looking ahead**

This is just the beginning, and it already points to where TV is headed. Custom, publisher-direct transactions that once demanded significant coordination, negotiation, and big budgets can now be planned, negotiated, and activated automatically putting premium inventory within reach of advertisers of every size. As this model evolves, the combination of human design and expertise, trusted relationships, and intelligent automation will define the next era of premium TV buying.

If you're an advertiser ready to transact with premium publishers on your terms, [book a demo here to learn more](https://www.universalads.com/book-a-demo).

results.title: Google Ads MCP: connect Claude to your ad account (2026)
results.markdown:
Title: Google Ads MCP: connect Claude to your ad account (2026)

URL Source: https://superscale.ai/learn/google-ads-mcp/

Published Time: 2026-07-23T13:26:36.000Z

Markdown Content:
_Updated July 23, 2026_

A Google Ads MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that connects an AI assistant like Claude to your Google Ads account, so you can pull performance reports, analyze campaigns, and launch new ads by typing a prompt instead of clicking through the Ads interface. Once it is connected, "show me last week's wasted spend" becomes a question you type in chat, not a report you build in the platform.

MCP is the open standard Anthropic released in November 2024 for connecting AI assistants to outside tools and data ([Anthropic's announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol?ref=superscale.ai)). An MCP server for ads applies that standard to ad platforms: the server exposes tools, Claude calls them, and your campaign data flows into the conversation.

This guide covers what a Google Ads MCP actually does, how to connect Claude to Google Ads with the Superscale AI MCP step by step, prompt examples you can paste today, an honest comparison of the servers available in 2026, and the limits nobody puts in their launch tweet.

## What is a Google Ads MCP?

The Model Context Protocol defines how an AI assistant discovers and calls external tools ([modelcontextprotocol.io](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/?ref=superscale.ai)). A Google Ads MCP server sits between the assistant and your ad account and translates chat requests into data operations. You ask a question in plain English, Claude picks the right tool, the server does the work, and the answer comes back as text and tables instead of a CSV export.

Two architectures dominate, and the difference matters more than any feature list.

**API wrappers** talk directly to the Google Ads API. You need a developer token, OAuth credentials from a Google Cloud project, and some comfort with configuration files ([Google Ads API docs](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/start?ref=superscale.ai)). In return you get raw query access: campaigns, ad groups, keywords, search terms, whatever the API exposes. Most open-source servers on GitHub work this way.

**Agent MCPs** connect Claude to a platform that already holds the ad account connection. Setup is a login instead of a cloud project, and you get the platform's capabilities as chat commands, not just raw data. Superscale AI's MCP is this type: Superscale connects to Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, Shopify, and Google Analytics, and the MCP server makes those connections available inside Claude. If the whole category of agents driving ad accounts is new to you, start with [what an AI marketing agent is](https://superscale.ai/learn/what-is-an-ai-marketing-agent/) and come back.

Four jobs cover most real usage.

1.   **Reporting.** Pull spend, conversions, CPA, and ROAS by campaign for any date range, and have Claude flag the outliers. The report you used to assemble every Monday morning becomes one sentence.

## Google Ads MCP prompt examples

These are starting points, not magic words. Adjust date ranges and thresholds to your account.

### Reporting prompts

```
Pull a Google Ads performance report for the last 30 days. Break it
down by campaign: spend, conversions, CPA, and ROAS. Flag every
campaign with a CPA more than 20 percent above the account average.
```

A report run costs 10 credits, a plain chat message 1, so the reporting habit is cheap to build.

### Analysis prompts

```
Compare my Google Ads and Meta results for the last quarter. Which
campaigns should I scale, which should I cut, and how would you
reallocate the budget between the two channels? Give reasons per line.
```

```
Research the ads my main competitor is running right now. Summarize
their hooks and offers, compare them to my active Google Ads creative,
and list the three biggest gaps I should test.
```

### Campaign iteration prompts

```
Take my three best performing ads from the last 30 days, generate five
new static variants of each in our brand style, and prepare them for
Google Ads in 1:1 and 16:9.
```

Static images cost 30 credits each and agent video runs 500 credits per 15 seconds, so batch deliberately. The follow-up testing discipline lives in our [campaign optimization guide](https://superscale.ai/learn/campaign-optimization-guide/).

### Automation prompts

```
Every Friday at 9am, pull the weekly performance summary across
Google Ads and Meta and post it to our Slack channel.
```
